at ryste på hovedet.explanation: "At ryste på hovedet" means "to shake one's head". It is built from "at ryste" (to shake) and "hovedet" (the head). To name what you shook your head at, add "ad" (at) before it: "Jeg rystede på hovedet ad hans svar" (I shook my head at his answer).

at råde over.explanation: "At råde over" means "to have at one's disposal". Without "over", the verb "at råde" means "to advise": "Jeg råder dig til at vente" (I advise you to wait).

at rådføre sig.explanation: "At rådføre sig" means "to consult". To name the person you consult, add "med" (with) before that person. After "jeg" (I), "sig" (oneself) becomes "mig" (myself): "Jeg rådfører mig med lægen" (I consult the doctor).

at rådne.explanation: "At rådne" means "to rot". The word for "rotten" is "rådden": "en rådden banan" (a rotten banana).

at række.explanation: "At række" means "to reach / hand". When you pass something to someone, say: "Kan du række mig saltet?" (Can you hand me the salt?). When you say there is enough of something, say: "Pengene rækker ikke" (The money is not enough).

at række hånden op.explanation: "At række hånden op" means "to raise one's hand". To say it is your own hand, Danish says "hånden" (the hand), not "min hånd" (my hand): "Hun rakte hånden op" (She raised her hand).

at rødme.explanation: "At rødme" means "to blush". It is built from "rød" (red). To say someone is red in the face from effort, use "rød i hovedet" (red in the face): "Han er rød i hovedet efter løbeturen" (He is red in the face after the run).

at røre.explanation: "At røre" means "to touch / stir". To say you stir food, say: "Rør i suppen" (Stir the soup). To say you touch something, add "ved" after the verb: "Rør ikke ved min telefon" (Do not touch my phone).

at røre rundt.explanation: "At røre rundt" means "to stir". "Rundt" means "around", and it also works with other verbs: "at gå rundt" (to walk around), "at køre rundt" (to drive around).

at røve.explanation: "At røve" means "to rob". To say someone takes something without threatening anyone, use "at stjæle" (to steal): "Nogen har stjålet min cykel" (Someone has stolen my bike).

en rabat.explanation: "En rabat" means "a discount". To ask for a discount, leave out "en": "Kan jeg få rabat?" (Can I get a discount?).

en race.explanation: "En race" means "a breed". To say a dog breed, join "hund" (dog) and "race": "en hunderace" (a dog breed). To say a running race, use "et løb" (a race): "Hun vandt løbet" (She won the race).

en radar.explanation: "En radar" means "a radar". To say something shows up on it, use "på radaren" (on the radar): "Flyet er på radaren" (The plane is on the radar).

en radiator.explanation: "En radiator" means "a radiator". To say you turn up the heat, say: "Jeg skruer op for radiatoren" (I turn up the radiator).

en radio.explanation: "En radio" means "a radio". To say something was on the radio, Danish says "i radioen" (literally, "in the radio"): "Det var i radioen" (It was on the radio).

en radioavis.explanation: "En radioavis" means "a radio news broadcast". It is built from "radio" (radio) and "avis" (newspaper). To say you read the printed paper, use "avis" alone: "Jeg læser avisen" (I read the newspaper).

en radius.explanation: "En radius" means "a radius". To say within a distance of a place, use "inden for en radius af" (within a radius of): "Alle butikker inden for en radius af to kilometer" (All shops within a radius of two kilometers).

en raket.explanation: "En raket" means "a rocket". When you talk about a firework that shoots into the sky, you also use "raket": "Han tændte en raket" (He lit a rocket).

en rang.explanation: "En rang" means "a rank". To describe a person of high standing, say: "en mand af høj rang" (a man of high rank).

en rangorden.explanation: "En rangorden" means "a ranking". It is built from "rang" (rank) and "orden" (order). To say a group of animals or people has a pecking order, use "en hakkeorden" (a pecking order): "Der er en hakkeorden blandt kollegerne" (There is a pecking order among the colleagues).

en rapport.explanation: "En rapport" means "a report". To say you write one, use "at skrive" (to write): "Jeg skriver en rapport" (I am writing a report).

en reaktion.explanation: "En reaktion" means "a reaction". To say what a reaction is about, use "på" (to): "en reaktion på nyheden" (a reaction to the news).

en recept.explanation: "En recept" means "a prescription". For a cooking recipe, use "en opskrift" (a recipe): "Jeg har en opskrift på kage" (I have a recipe for cake).

en reception.explanation: "En reception" means "a reception desk". It also means a party where guests are received: "Vi holder reception på fredag" (We are holding a reception on Friday).
